mt_amphitheater_area.blurb: A winter cliff in Hyalite Canyon above Bozeman, with water ice and a dense cluster of dry-tooling and mixed lines. Of the 19 climbs, most are mixed, running from around M4 up to M11, and the ice is mainly WI3 and WI4. It is one of the easier ice venues in the canyon to reach, so it draws both newer ice climbers and people just coming to watch. Expect company on good weekends. Sun and shade are not recorded here, and conditions depend entirely on the freeze, so check the current ice report before heading up.
mt_amphitheater_area.approach: Follow the main Grotto Falls trail south from the trailhead, and where it forks the cliff is just off to the left.

mt_foyer_the.blurb: A sport crag within Natural Bridge and Falls, tucked into a canyon in south-central Montana. All 19 routes are bolted. The west side holds the gentler lines, around 5.6 to 5.9, which makes it the usual place to warm up. The east side steepens and carries the harder routes, mostly 5.11 and 5.12 with a single 5.13. Reaching the wall means crossing the large bridge, following the canyon rim, and dropping through a small slot and a scrambly corridor. A good stop for a mixed-ability group, with warm-ups and projects within a few steps of each other.

mt_queen_north_face.blurb: The shadier side of the Queen formation at Spire Rock, in the Butte area of southwest Montana. Mostly trad, with a couple of top-rope lines and one sport route among the 19 climbs. Grades start near 5.6 and cluster around 5.7 to 5.10, with a handful of harder lines reaching into the 5.12s and 5.13. The wall has plenty of crack climbing and suits climbers wanting a first real rope-length of rock. A gully on the side makes it easy to walk up and rig top ropes, or you can build anchors with gear. The north side is cooler and more relaxed than the south.

mt_south_jersey_shore.blurb: A wall of fine-grained limestone in Big Bear Canyon, near Bozeman, holding 19 sport routes. They are long, technical and crimpy, and the grades start around 5.10 and run mostly through 5.11 and 5.12 into low 5.13, which makes it a stop for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. It faces mostly north, unlike the other walls in the canyon, and stays out of the sun until mid-afternoon in summer, so it works on hot days and mornings are best. Bring plenty of draws and a helmet for the belayer, as some lines see little traffic.

mt_elk_rock.blurb: A forested cliff in the Lolo area near Missoula, with an unusually varied mix. Of its 19 climbs, twelve are trad and seven are sport. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.11, with the most common range around 5.10. Offerings include easy multi-pitch trad routes alongside older, harder sport lines whose small bolts are spaced far apart. Natural protection can take some thought, and tricams get a good workout. The setting is shaded and wooded without being dense, which makes for pleasant cragging, though the older bolted routes deserve a careful eye.

mt_big_creek_mccalla_ridge.blurb: A remote crag in the Bitterroot foothills south of Missoula, higher than most of the valley's crags and often windy. Fourteen of the 18 routes are bolted and four are trad, with grades from 5.9 up to a single 5.13, though most sit between 5.10 and 5.11. The rock is solid and offers cracks, thin crimps and some slab. Walls mostly face south and west, so they catch plenty of sun. The sidehill walk from the road is short, and the crowds are thin, making it a good spot for a quiet day when other Bitterroot crags are busy.

mt_overhangatang_boulders.blurb: A small cluster of boulders right beside the road in Hyalite Canyon, south of Bozeman, sitting a bit over a mile above Practice Rock. The 18 problems cover a wide span, with a few at V0, a group around V3, and then a steady climb of harder lines up to V10. There are not many problems, but the quality is high, and the steeper lines reward strong boulderers. Because the area is so compact it suits a short session or a stop on the way to other Hyalite crags. The pullout beside the boulders only holds a few cars.

mt_style_wall.blurb: A limestone wall on a long fin in Rattler Gulch, east of Missoula, mostly bolted. Of 18 routes, thirteen are sport, four trad and one top-rope. Grades range from about 5.8 to 5.12, but the bulk are 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable on moderate-to-hard sport. The wall stays cool and shaded in the heat of summer, which is the main reason to come. Some of the rock is loose, and routes may have small crumbly sections, so a helmet is wise. The walk up from the cars is short, with the first routes only a short way along the trail.
